title: Fpqc reflection of the effective Cartier condition for a specified ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $i:T\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_T)$ be its quasi-coherent ideal sheaf with its specified inclusion into $\mathcal O_X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Let $\{g_a:Y_a\to X\}_{a\in A}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Put $T_a=T\times_XY_a$ and let $q_a:T_a\to Y_a$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose that every ideal $\mathcal J_a=\ker(\mathcal O_{Y_a}\to(q_a)_*\mathcal O_{T_a})$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then the canonical maps $g_a^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{Y_a}$ [def-pc-module-pullback] identify $g_a^*\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal J_a$, and $\mathcal I$ is locally free of rank one as an $\mathcal O_X$-module, hence an invertible ideal [def-nagata-invertible-ideal] and an effective Cartier ideal. The conclusion allows the unit ideal and requires no reducedness, local Noetherianity or etaleness.

source.place: Tag 05B2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-descends), with Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent) and literature/stacks-project/divisors.tex Tag 01WS (lemma-characterize-effective-Cartier-divisor); the ideal inclusion is retained when applying rank-one descent. Extracted from item proof step 3.

proof.text: Each g_a is flat by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The Mathlib kernel base-change identity Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion, transported by pullback symmetry, gives ker(q_a) = I.comap(g_a), with I the specified kernel ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Apply [lem-pur-ideal-tensor-pullback-comparison] to this ideal. Its canonical factor d is an isomorphism by flatness, and its defining equality is exactly the required equality after composition with the specified inclusion. Taking asIso d supplies the isomorphism in the first conclusion.

For each covering ideal J_a, apply the already proved IdealSheafData.IsInvertible.isInvertible_toModules in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.EffectiveCartier to its nonzerodivisor local generators [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. This is the multiplication-by-a-generator construction of Stacks 01WS. Pass from scheme-module invertibility to sheaf-module invertibility by [lem-pc-invertible-sheaf-instance], then use the rank-one equivalence for [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Transport finite local freeness of rank one across the isomorphism from step 1 and the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism between tensorPullback(g_a) and pullback(g_a).

Apply fixed-rank fpqc descent [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to M=I.toModules and its own canonical descent datum (modulesPseudofunctor.toDescentData g).obj M, with the identity as the comparison isomorphism. The precoverage membership gives covering-sieve membership by Precoverage.generate_mem_toGrothendieck. Step 2 supplies the rank-one condition on each component. Thus the original specified module is finite locally free of rank one. The general descent declaration used here also derives quasi-coherence from the finite locally free covering components; no independent quasi-coherence lemma or compatible choice of bases is required.

proof.text: Use the rank-one equivalence [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] to regard I.toModules as an invertible sheaf-module. At each point choose an affine neighbourhood U and a free generator s [def-sc-local-free-generator], using the proved exists_isFreeGenerator. Set t = I.toModulesι.app U s. If a*t=0, linearity of the ideal inclusion and its injectivity on sections imply a*s=0; freeness of s implies a=0. Hence t is a nonzerodivisor. Every element of I.ideal U lifts to a module section by range_toModulesι_app, and every such section is r*s. Thus I.ideal U is contained in (t). Conversely t lies in I.ideal U, so (t) is contained in it. This proves local regular principality, namely [def-nagata-invertible-ideal] and [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. This argument includes t=1 and is vacuous on the empty scheme.

lean.statement: theorem fpqc_cartier_ideal_reflection {X T : Scheme.{u}} (i : T ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] {A : Type w} (Y : A → Scheme.{u}) (g : ∀ a : A, Y a ⟶ X) (hg : Presieve.ofArrows Y g ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage X) (hJ : ∀ a : A, (pullback.snd i (g a)).ker.IsInvertible) : (∀ a : A, ∃ e : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (g a)).obj i.ker.toModules ≅ (pullback.snd i (g a)).ker.toModules, e.hom ≫ (pullback.snd i (g a)).ker.toModulesι = (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (g a)).map i.ker.toModulesι ≫ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit (g a)) ∧ i.ker.toModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1 ∧ i.ker.IsInvertible
